excluded.injury_adm_12m: measured after adherence (months 7-18); used only as a negative-control outcome, never as a control

ldl_baseline.meaning: LDL cholesterol (mg/dL) when the statin was prescribed

admits_prior_yr.meaning: All-cause hospital admissions in the year before prescription; the closest thing to a before-the-action measure of the outcome

flu_shot_prior_yr.meaning: 1 = flu vaccination in the year before prescription; a partial stand-in for health-seeking behaviour

adherent.meaning: 1 = statin filled for at least 80% of days in the first 6 months (proportion of days covered >= 80%)

cardiac_adm_12m.meaning: 1 = admitted for a cardiac event in the following 12 months

injury_adm_12m.meaning: 1 = admitted for an accidental injury in the following 12 months; a statin cannot plausibly prevent this

domain_notes.domain: statin adherence and cardiac hospital admissions (health insurer claims)

known_traps.name: Healthy-adherer effect
known_traps.why: People who take their medicines as prescribed also tend to exercise, eat better, keep appointments and avoid risks, so they have fewer admissions of every kind, whether or not the pill works. Classic evidence: adherent statin users also had fewer road accidents and workplace injuries (Dormuth et al., Circulation 2009), and people who took their placebo faithfully in trials lived longer.
known_traps.handled: Prior flu vaccination used as a partial stand-in control; accidental-injury admissions used as a negative-control outcome; the unrecorded part is drawn in the diagram and sized in the hidden-factor chart.

known_traps.name: Sick-stopper / reverse causation
known_traps.why: Members who become frail or ill early on may stop filling prescriptions, and are also more likely to be admitted, which makes non-adherence look harmful.
known_traps.handled: Prior-year admissions and baseline risk factors are controlled; the 6-month adherence window ends before the 12-month outcome window starts, which avoids counting early events. Remaining risk noted as a question.

known_traps.name: Adherence is not the programme
known_traps.why: Finance's number is for a programme of reminder calls; the programme will only make some non-adherent members adherent, so the effect of the programme is smaller than the effect of adherence.
known_traps.handled: Stated in the report; the result is the effect of adherence itself, an upper guide for the programme.

suspected_hidden.label: Health-conscious habits
suspected_hidden.why: Healthy-adherer effect: people who stick to their pills also look after their health in ways the claims data do not record (diet, exercise, alcohol, keeping appointments).

negative_control_outcomes.why: A statin cannot plausibly prevent accidental-injury admissions, but health-conscious habits could. An apparent 'effect' of adherence on injuries would expose healthy-adherer bias.

expected_effect.basis: Randomised trials (Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' meta-analyses) show statins cut major vascular events by roughly a fifth per 1 mmol/L LDL reduction, i.e. roughly 20-30% relative. On this file's roughly 11% one-year cardiac admission rate that is about 1 to 3.5 points; comparing >=80% vs <80% days covered (non-adherent members still take some tablets) and a one-year horizon push it toward the lower end. Written before the run.

alternatives.name: Without the flu-shot stand-in
alternatives.why: shows how much the one recorded health-seeking proxy moves the answer; if dropping it moves the answer a lot, unrecorded habits likely move it too

alternatives.name: Treat injury admissions as a control
alternatives.why: illustrates the trap of controlling for something measured after adherence

dismissed_findings.flu_shot_prior_yr: recorded in the year before the prescription (brief)
